title: Redwood December 2026 All-Hands
next_steps: Leadership to publish Q4 results summary doc by 2026-12-24
People Ops to send holiday shutdown calendar and on-call rotation by 2026-12-23
Product to share detailed roadmap timeline for H1 2027 by 2027-01-05

Luis: Run final NVMe+GPU performance test and post results in #infra (due 2026-12-30)

summary: CEO Claire Bennett opened with a brief financial and product update: strong Q4 bookings, cautious outlook on cloud GPU pricing, and focus on predictable inference economics. Leadership reviewed H1 2027 priorities— improving latency, launching a private on-prem package, and investing in Redwood Optimize features. People and hiring updates included a conservative headcount approach for Q1 and holiday coverage. The all-hands ended with clear next steps and action items around publishing roadmaps, benchmarks, and operational plans.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-22 | Start: 09:00 PST | Duration: 60m | Location: All-hands (Zoom) | Attendees: ~150
transcript:
[00:00] Claire Bennett: Good morning everyone, welcome to the December all-hands. I know it's a busy week, thanks for making time. We will run about 60 minutes, we'll cover Q4 highlights, product roadmap for H1, and some people ops items.
[00:22] Marcus Li: Quick note, recording is on, so if you have any sensitive info please use the slack thread later.
[00:35] Priya Singh: I'll jump into the roadmap after Claire, I have a 15-minute section.
[00:45] Claire Bennett: OK, first up, high level — Q4 bookings beat plan, we saw a nice uptick in mid-market renewals and a couple of strategic Dedicated deals. Revenue headroom looks solid but we are seeing cloud GPU price pressure pushing some customers to explore Dedicated or Private.
[01:12] Claire Bennett: We closed two Dedicated contracts this month, both on 12-month reserved capacity, combined ARR roughly equivalent to $1.2M annualized, will be in the finance deck. There was a question about gross margin — margins improved modestly on caching/Optimize but we still need more efficiency on long-tail requests.
[01:40] Luis Ortega: On infra, we shipped the NVMe-backed cache nodes to three clusters and saw a 12 to 20 percent P99 latency improvement for 2k seq workloads in internal tests. Caveat — workload distribution is uneven so results vary.
[01:58] Claire Bennett: That's promising. Can we get a consistent benchmark across models and sequence lengths?
[02:05] Luis Ortega: Yes, we're compiling a matrix and we'll publish it to Console and the internal benchmarks repo. Tomoko is helping with the customer-facing summary.
[02:18] Tomoko Sato: Yep, I'll consolidate findings into a short FAQ and a spreadsheet for customers who ask about Dedicated perf.
[02:26] [03:00] Claire Bennett: On product, Priya?
[03:05] Priya Singh: Thanks. Big picture for H1 2027 — three themes: 1) Reduce tail latency and improve predictability, 2) Launch Private V1 with tighter KMS/HSM integration, 3) Expand Redwood Optimize with model-quantization profiles and auto-batching suggestions.
[03:35] Priya Singh: For Private V1, target is an early access program in Feb with two pilot customers and GA late Q2. The plan includes a hardened deployment playbook and a pre-built KMS connector for AWS and GCP HSMs.
[03:54] Marcus Li: Important to note, Private V1 won't include on-prem air-gapped installs at GA; that's a later milestone. We want to be realistic about scope.
[04:07] Priya Singh: Right. We're focusing on VPC/private control plane first.
[04:13] [05:00] Claire Bennett: Questions on that?
[05:07] Speaker 1: Hey, is there an impact to Hosted pricing or quotas?
[05:13] Priya Singh: No direct change to hosted pricing; we expect some customers to move workloads to Dedicated or Private for cost reasons, but hosted remains our fastest path. We'll publish guidance.
[05:26] Claire Bennett: On the reliability front — Marcus?
[05:30] Marcus Li: We're investing in smarter routing and eviction policies for cache TTLs. Also automating fallback to smaller model variants when capacity is constrained — to avoid 503 cascades. We ran a pilot that reduced error rates during simulated region outages by ~45 percent. Caveat: smaller variants degrade quality on open-ended prompts, so product will flag potential quality regressions.
[05:58] [06:30] Claire Bennett: People ops — Hannah?
[06:35] Hannah Cole: Quick update: we will institute a short hiring freeze for non-critical IC roles from Jan 1 to Mar 31. Exceptions will be considered for mission-critical roles and sales quota hires. We'll circulate a form for managers to request exceptions. Also holiday coverage — skeleton on-call and support teams will cover Dec 24–27 and Dec 31–Jan 2.
[07:02] Claire Bennett: Please do make sure on-call handoffs are documented.
[07:07] Hannah Cole: Agreed, leads will post rosters by EOD tomorrow.
[07:12] [08:00] Claire Bennett: Quick product demo highlight — Priya, show one slide?
[08:06] Priya Singh: (screen shares) This is the Optimize UI mock; it suggests batching configs and recommended quant profiles per model. The idea is to present cost/latency trade-offs and let customers apply suggestions with one click.
[08:35] Speaker 2: How accurate are suggestions?
[08:39] Priya Singh: We're using internal evals and historical request traces; expected accuracy is high for throughput-heavy workloads but lower for low-volume, high-variance usage. We'll warn customers when confidence is low.
[09:02] [09:30] Claire Bennett: Security/compliance quick update — Marcus?
[09:35] Marcus Li: SOC 2 renewal is in progress, auditors on site in early Jan. We completed required evidence for access controls and are closing two findings around logging consistency. We plan to harden audit logs and improve retention settings in Console.
[09:56] Claire Bennett: Good. Any updates on SSO or SCIM?
[10:00] Marcus Li: SCIM provisioning is in beta and a handful of customers are testing; GA target is Feb.
[10:07] [11:00] Claire Bennett: Open Q&A — typed questions in chat, I'll read a few. First: "What is the hiring plan for Sales?"
[11:10] Claire Bennett: Sales will continue to hire quota-carrying reps in Q1 but we'll be cautious on SDR expansion.
[11:18] Speaker 3: "Are we planning price increases?"
[11:22] Claire Bennett: No across-the-board price hikes planned. We may rationalize packaging for enterprise add-ons and tighten quota tiers. We'll share more when the finance team finalizes.
[11:35] [12:00] Claire Bennett: Another question: "Will we support on-prem air-gapped customers?"
[12:08] Marcus Li: Long term yes, but that's post-GA for Private. It's a large engineering lift that requires dedicated QA and security reviews.
[12:18] [13:00] Priya Singh: I want to call out two launches for Jan: (1) a new model catalog view in Console with performance profiles, and (2) an improved streaming API that reduces startup latency for chat scenarios. Both are early Jan targets but may slip depending on test results.
[13:36] Claire Bennett: Please make sure the docs team is looped early.
[13:42] [14:00] Luis Ortega: One more infra note — we're testing a kernel selection optimization that chooses faster kernels for specific attention patterns; early runs show 8–10% per-token CPU reduction. We'll need to validate across 7B/13B/70B model shapes.
[14:25] Claire Bennett: Nice.
[14:30] [15:00] Hannah Cole: Quick people note — thank you for the end-of-year charity matches and volunteer events. We had great participation. Also reminders to submit dice-rolledes for manager calibration by Jan 10. (transcription: "dice-rolledes" likely meant "comp-rankings", hmm)
[15:34] Claire Bennett: Ha, yes, and HR will clarify the exact term in the follow-up.
[15:40] [16:00] Claire Bennett: We have about ten minutes left — I'll recap next steps: publish the Q4 summary, Product to share H1 roadmap, Eng to publish benchmarks, People Ops to send holiday/on-call rosters.
[16:18] Claire Bennett: Thank you all for a huge year. Quick shoutout to the infra and SRE teams for keeping incident rates down during our busiest runs.
[16:34] Marcus Li: Thank you everyone.
[16:38] [17:00] Claire Bennett: OK we'll wrap. Enjoy the holidays, see you in Jan.
[17:06] (meeting ends)
